items_missed: No 'How are you today?' opener
Didn't get the customer's name until roughly eight minutes in, when he needed it for the email - the whole quote was delivered to a stranger
Never checked availability for September 11
No agenda statement and no 'sound good?' confirmation
Never asked about additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony, patio)
Never asked about special considerations - long walks, narrow hallways, tight turns
Never asked how many boxes
Never asked about storage stops or additional stops
Never asked about moving stressors
No 'pricing is super simple' opener
Meet Your Mover not delivered - he said 'we'll know the quality of the crew ahead of your move day' but never described the pre-move email with the mover's photo and info
On-Time Guarantee named only in passing ('we have a [on-time] guarantee') with no explanation that Einstein starts discounting if it misses the window
Entire clock section skipped - no clock-starts-on-site, no 2.5 hour minimum, no 15-minute prorated increments, no sense-check
No walk-distance discussion (customer is moving building-to-building across a complex) and no size equivalents to make the 26-foot truck concrete
Save Your Ass never attempted - not one word about prep shortening the move or lowering the bill
No attempt to book - 'once you're ready to book we can do it either way you want' put it entirely on the customer
Never said no deposit is required
No bolded detail list at the top of the email, no 'reply with any corrections'
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
No hours or how-to-reach-us
Never used the customer's name once, even after collecting it
No 60 cents/lb baseline alongside the $2,000 coverage
Quoted the price before collecting addresses, unit numbers, or square footage - the math error ($360, self-corrected to $660) came out of quoting that early
top_strength: He handled a customer who asked the same packing question four different ways with real patience and clarity - he set an honest expectation that packing roughly doubles the time, priced the supplies at about $200, drew a clean line on what's included (takes the TV down, won't remount it; reassembles what they disassemble, won't unpack boxes), and offered to send the estimate with packing and without so the customer could compare.
coaching_note: He quoted a price in the first ninety seconds off nothing but bedroom count and floor, then spent the rest of the call back-filling details he should have gathered first - no box count, no additional rooms, no walk distance, no stressors. Complete the probe before the number leaves your mouth, and add the clock explanation and Save Your Ass speech, which were both skipped entirely and are worth 14 points on their own.
phone_presence_notes: Clear, patient, and personable in spots (the Texas-heat line about tipping, and a graceful self-correction on the math), but he never used the customer's name, never acknowledged that moving is stressful, and let the customer drive the whole conversation.
